documents.t: The elves of the Fey Wood

Lorandal is a single large continent, about 700 miles east to west and 500 miles north to south, comparable in size to France and Spain combined. The Kingdom of Zeref holds the central and eastern majority. The Fey Wood, home of the elves, covers the northwest. The Greylands lie behind the Iron Wall mountains in the southwest. Offshore are a lone volcanic island in the Dragon Sea to the southeast and, far across the eastern ocean, the continent of Kethara.

The Fey Wilds is the name travelers give to the deep interior of the Fey Wood, beyond the border regions that ordinary maps attempt to show. Accounts from the handful of outsiders who have crossed into it agree on one point: the deep forest behaves less like a stand of trees than like something aware of who walks its paths.
Beyond its cities, Lorandal holds a handful of places every traveler learns to name: a poisoned battlefield, a forbidden ruin, a sheltered harbor, and old forests best left to themselves.

Background on the world of Lorandal: its lands and history, the gods its peoples keep, the powers that divide the continent, and the great festival on the horizon.

Lorandal is the main continent of the known world, about 700 miles east to west and 500 miles north to south. The Kingdom of Zeref controls almost all of it. Two other continents are known: Kethara across the eastern sea, and an unnamed western landmass that no expedition has ever successfully explored.

Three powers divide the continent of Lorandal: the Kingdom of Zeref, which holds nearly all of it; the elves of the Fey Wood in the northwest; and the clans of the Greylands, sealed behind the Iron Wall in the southwest.

The Kingdom of Zeref was founded three thousand years ago and has been ruled by a single unbroken royal line ever since. Most of what happened before and during the founding era has been lost; the record below is what the Kingdom itself teaches and keeps.

The peoples of Lorandal keep a broad and living faith. Each of the founding races honors its own creator god, and above and alongside them stands a wider pantheon worshipped across the whole Kingdom of Zeref.

The Kingdom of Zeref has been race-blind in law for three thousand years. In practice, its population reflects its history: humans form the majority everywhere, elves are vanishingly rare, and Ironhold is the one city where dwarves outnumber everyone else.

Once every 500 years the moon rises blue for a single night, and the world stops to celebrate it. The priesthood of Lyssa, goddess of luck, has claimed the omen as hers for as long as records go back, and the festival held under the blue light has grown into the largest celebration anyone knows: lanterns in every window, banners down every street, and a wish made, by tradition, by the whole world at once.

The Fey Wilds is the name travelers give to the deep interior of the Fey Wood, beyond the border regions that ordinary maps attempt to show. Accounts from the handful of outsiders who have crossed into it agree on one point: the deep forest behaves less like a stand of trees than like something aware of who walks its paths.

Effect Description Time distortion Time inside does not always match time outside. Travelers have emerged to find more, or less, time passed in the world than they experienced. Misdirection Without a Sylvan speaker or a fey guide, travelers drift from their intended path without noticing. Heightened magic Magic is consistently reported to behave more strongly inside the deep forest. Awareness The forest notices visitors quickly, and its creatures sense mortals long before mortals sense them.

Kingdom maps of the Fey Wilds are unreliable and have been for three thousand years. The forest is known to rearrange its own paths, and sometimes whole landmarks, to confuse anyone who means it harm. The western coast, called The Veil, is permanently wrapped in mist and has never been charted at all.

Arendale is the only confirmed point of contact between the Kingdom and the elves, open one day a year for the annual trade. The Mist Gate, further north, is watched at all times by the Mist Watch garrison on the Kingdom side; crossing there is a matter of politics rather than geography. Travelers who wander into the forest without a guide should expect it to have its own opinion about where they end up.
Beyond its cities, Lorandal holds a handful of places every traveler learns to name: a poisoned battlefield, a forbidden ruin, a sheltered harbor, and old forests best left to themselves.

A vast blighted waste near the center of the Kingdom, a scar left from the age of the founding that has never healed. Nothing grows across it, and nothing has in living memory. Farmers work its outer edges out of necessity and avoid its heart, and the old accounts always name it in the same breath as the ruins of Valdris.

An abandoned city within reach of the Ash Fields, ruined in the age of the founding and never rebuilt. Royal decree forbids anyone to enter it, though the decree hardly needs enforcing: the place has an ill name, something is rumored to den among the ruins, and those who ignore the warning and go in have a habit of not coming out.

The deep, sheltered western bay on whose northern shore Karth stands. Its protected waters are the reason the city exists; they serve as a naval staging ground and receive the single elven trade ship that comes each year from Arendale.
A worked timber forest between Karth and Varenholm, harvested and replanted for generations and entirely ordinary, whatever the old stories say about displacer beasts prowling its deep interior.

An ancient wild forest spreading between Varenholm, Redcross, Coppergate, and Tidefall. Its edges are logged, but its old-growth heart is left alone, home to bears, dire wolves, and, if the stories are true, owlbears. Locals swear a circle of druids keeps to its depths.

The Crown's trained ravens are the fastest link in the kingdom, crossing most of it within a day or two, and royal couriers with remounts cover about 70 miles a day on the main roads. Even so, the capital always governs on news that is days old: a courier from Karth takes roughly five days to reach Azriel. In the south, sea travel is faster than land by a wide margin; Karth to Tidefall takes three days by ship against nine or more overland, which is why coastal trade dominates the southern economy.

The continent divides into a handful of broad regions. Below is a guide to each, and what lies within it. For distances between them, see Travel and Distances; for the full list of towns, see Settlements.

The core of the Kingdom, strung along the King's River as it runs south from Crown Lake to the sea. This is the realm's political and commercial spine: the capital at Azriel on Crown Lake, the great bridge-city of Varenholm, and the self-governing town of Millhaven, with smaller river towns such as Redcross and Crossfen between them. Barges run the river day and night, and the corridor's cities raise most of the Kingdom's coin. The worked timberland of the Grey Wood runs along the corridor's western edge.

Where the Kingdom meets the open sea. Karth, the busiest port in the realm, sits on Golden Harbor and takes in most of the traffic arriving by water, including the single elven trade ship that comes each year from Arendale. Beyond its walls lie the Harbor Plains that feed the city.

The warm, wealthy shore where the Southern Reach comes to Lorandal. Tidefall is the cosmopolitan gateway for southern trade, and Saltmere, west along the coast, is the home port of the Kingdom's fleet. East of Tidefall lies the Dragon Sea, feared and little sailed.

The Kingdom's mining country, in the foothills and passes of the World Spine. Ironhold, the only dwarven city, works the mountains alongside the gnome engineers of Coppergate, while the garrison at East Gate watches the eastern trade road and the trails beyond. The Royal Hills rise between here and the capital. Sunfall sits on Mirror Lake at the region's western edge, the farming village of Harrow lies south toward the Southrun, and the old-growth Ashwood spreads between them.

Stormhaven stands alone on the Storm Sea, the Kingdom's only northern port and its summer link to Kethara. The road north from Azriel runs through Crestfall to reach it. For half the year winter closes the sea, and the city turns in on itself.

A wide blighted waste near the center of the Kingdom where nothing grows, and nothing has in living memory. Farmers work its edges out of necessity and shun its heart, and the ruined places within it, chief among them the dead city of Valdris, which the crown forbids anyone to enter, are left well alone. See Landmarks and Wild Places.

The elven northwest: an ancient forest that resists mapping and rearranges its own paths. The Kingdom knows only its fringe, the trade town of Arendale, open one day a year, and the names of settlements deeper in, such as the capital Moonveil, that no outsider has seen. At the forest's heart stands the Elder Tree, the elves' most sacred site, which no outsider has laid eyes on. On the Kingdom's side of the treeline, the garrison at Mist Watch keeps watch over the Mist Gate. The mist-wrapped coast of The Veil borders the wood to the west. See The Fey Wilds.

Harsh, poor country behind the Iron Wall in the southwest, held by the clans of Grimhold. Two passes, Iron Pass in the north and Stone Pass in the south, are the only ways through the mountains, and the Kingdom's garrisons have held them against Greylands raids for three thousand years. See The Greylands.

Four seas ring the continent. The Veil, off the elven coast to the west, is calm but wrapped in permanent mist. The Storm Sea to the north is dangerous the year round. The Dragon Sea to the east is feared and little sailed, and holds a lone volcanic island. Only the Southern Reach itself is reliably calm, and it carries most of the Kingdom's long-distance trade. Closer in, Golden Harbor shelters Karth in the west, while Irondeep Bay, walled off by mountains in the northeast, sees no honest traffic.
East across the Southern Reach lies Kethara, the six-race realm the departing dwarves helped found long ago. Far to the west lies a barren, unmapped continent that explorers do not return from.

Aldric Zeref Title King of Zeref Race Human Age 30s Reign CY ~2890 to present Predecessor Davan Zeref Consort Queen Sera Zeref Seat The Royal Palace, Azriel Aldric Zeref is the reigning King of Zeref, about a decade into his rule. He is the son of Davan Zeref and the latest of a royal line three thousand years old. Aldric is lean and sharp-featured, more scholar than soldier to look at, and what authority he carries is in his manner. In public he keeps to the formal; in private, by the accounts of those close to him, he is a good deal warmer. He is widely thought a genuinely good king, and he has no heir, a matter of quiet and growing concern at court. His most trusted advisor is Vaelith, the Crown Mage, whose counsel he weighs above any other. Like every king before him, Aldric upholds the ancient law that keeps the elves apart from the Kingdom; it is the world he inherited.

Bram Coldwell Title Chancellor Race Halfling Age 40s Council seat Administration Bram Coldwell rose to Chancellor young, remarkably so for a halfling, and wears the office lightly: pragmatic, warm, and quick with a joke in a chamber not known for them. King Aldric trusts him without reservation. He and Treasury Master Sella Wickmore are old friends, and between them they run most of the Kingdom's daily administration.

Brennan Morse Role Sergeant, Karth city watch Post The north gate Race Human Brennan Morse is a sergeant of the Karth city watch, stationed at the north gate. The party first crossed paths with him there during the disturbance on the festival night, and came away with a low opinion of his conduct under pressure.

Caedan Voss Title Supreme Commander Race Human Age Mid-50s Council seat Military Caedan Voss has commanded the Kingdom's armies for a decade, and made his name long before that holding the Greylands passes, where no officer in the kingdom is his equal at siege and garrison warfare. His loyalty runs to the Kingdom before the man who wears the crown; he respects King Aldric as his king without pretending to be his friend. He is a commander of hard conviction who does not change course lightly, and he has never hidden that a fortification suits him better than a court.

Castor Varen Title Lord of House Varen Race Human Age 50s Daughter Queen Sera Zeref Residence Crown Quarter, Azriel Castor Varen is the head of House Varen, one of Azriel's old court families, and the father of Queen Sera Zeref. He is in his fifties and at the height of his influence. Castor has a reputation as a cold strategist whose family affection, though real, always seems to come second to position. His network of allies and clients runs through most of Azriel's official class, and little happens in the Crown Quarter that he does not hear about.

Dolgrin Stonemantle Title Master of Records Race Dwarf Age Late 200s Seat The Hall of Records, Azriel Dolgrin Stonemantle has kept the Hall of Records in Azriel longer than anyone now living, through the reigns of more kings than most people could name. He values the stability of the Kingdom above all else and is precise to a fault; he answers a careful, specific question far more readily than an urgent one, and scholars who arrive at the Hall unprepared tend to leave with very little.

Gura Stoneback Title Harbor Master General Race Orc Age Early 50s Council seat Naval affairs Gura Stoneback came up through a naval family that has crewed and captained the Kingdom's fleets for generations, and now holds the naval seat on the council as an elder by orcish reckoning. She is blunt and direct, with no agenda anyone has ever managed to turn up, and she measures her career in ships built, engagements won, and sailors brought home alive. King Aldric is said to keep her close for exactly that plainness.

Pell Ashwick Title Crown Mage of Karth Race Human Age 30s Residence Karth Pell Ashwick is the Crown Mage of Karth: brilliant with instruments and hopeless with people, in about that order. Her workroom is full of devices of her own design and some of the most meticulous arcane records anyone in her position keeps. She is the one to find in Karth for careful, patient answers to strange questions, if a visitor can get her to look up from her readings.

Sella Wickmore Title Treasury Master Race Gnome Age 40s Council seat Finance Sella Wickmore keeps the Kingdom's accounts, and keeps them to the copper, however scattered she may seem across a dinner table. Barely an adult by gnomish reckoning, she has centuries of the work still ahead of her. More than one visiting merchant has taken the cheerful, distracted surface for the whole of her and regretted it. She and Chancellor Bram Coldwell are the oldest of friends.

Sera Zeref Title Queen Consort of Zeref Race Human Age 30s Born Sera Varen, Azriel Spouse King Aldric Zeref Father Lord Castor Varen Sera Zeref, born Sera Varen, is the Queen Consort of Zeref and one of the shrewdest political operators in the citadel. Sera was raised in one of Azriel's old court families and reads the politics of the capital better than her husband does. She is composed at all times in public and reveals nothing she does not intend to. Her marriage to Aldric is understood to be a genuine partnership. She remains close to her father, Lord Castor Varen, who prepared her for court life from childhood.

Sorath Status Deceased First seen Karth, north gate Origin Unknown Sorath was a stranger who appeared at Karth's north gate on the night the party first gathered there. He gave only the single name before events overtook him, and where he came from, and what he was, remain unknown. Sorath fought beside the party against the creatures that came out of the ground that night, and died out on the Harbor Plains before it was over. He spoke, at the end, in a tongue none of them recognized. The party were among the few who saw it, and none of them can say what they saw.

Vaelith Title Crown Mage of Azriel Race Human Service Under King Davan, then King Aldric Seat The Crown Mage's Tower, Azriel Vaelith is the Crown Mage of Azriel, the highest magical authority in the Kingdom of Zeref and the closest advisor to the throne. She heads the order of Crown Mages, and every city's Crown Mage answers to her. She served under King Davan before Aldric, and no counsel carries more weight with the crown than hers. Even by the standards of court mages she keeps to herself. Her tower in the Citadel is one of the city's landmarks, its upper floors sealed and closed to visitors, and she is seldom seen far from it. See The Council of Azriel for the court she sits above.

Arendale Population ~8,000 Type Elven coastal trade town Region Fey Wood northwestern coast, The Veil Governance Elven council authority; Harbormaster Leth Notable sites The Annual Trade Dock Arendale is the only elven settlement the Kingdom of Zeref has ever confirmed exists. A coastal town on the northwestern edge of the Fey Wood, it is the elves' sole official point of contact with the outside world, and outsiders may lay eyes on it just one day a year, when the concealment that hides the town is lifted for the annual trade. The town is unlike any Kingdom settlement. Its buildings grow with the trees rather than displacing them, and its streets are closer to forest paths. Arendale's residents belong to the younger, engagement-minded side of elven society; they deal with the Kingdom deliberately and on their own terms, and visitors describe them as watchful and precise rather than hostile. The town keeps a great temple of Melora, goddess of the wild and the sea.

Once a year, on a date set jointly by the Crown and the Council of Elders, one elven ship sails from Arendale to Karth and one Kingdom ship sails from Karth to Arendale. If either ship fails to return, the agreement is permanently broken. The kingdom ship's berth stands empty and maintained the other 364 days of the year. Harbormaster Leth manages the trade on the elven side, and is the most accessible entry point into elven society that any Kingdom visitor is likely to find.

District Description The Harbor The working waterfront, built around the annual trade. The Settlement Proper Homes and common houses among the trees. The Forest Edge Where Arendale meets the deeper Fey Wood.

Name Description The Harbour Hearth The only inn that regularly hosts non-elves. The Still Branch An elven common house; rooms extended to outsiders only when someone vouches for them. The Trade Table A working tavern active only during the trade window.

Ashford Population ~4,200 Type Supply town Region Northwest, on the Mist Road Governance Administrator Holt Varen Notable sites The Wellkeep Spring Ashford is a quiet farming town on the Mist Road, and the main supplier of the Mist Watch garrison further north. Little of the crown reaches it beyond its administrator. The town is best known locally for the Wellkeep Spring, a handsome stone basin in the town square fed by an underground source. The spring is the town's water supply and its quiet point of pride, and it has been maintained by the Wellkeep family for six generations.

District Description The Town Square The center of Ashford. The spring, the daily market, and the Millstone Inn. The Supply Quarter Warehouses and the liaison post serving Mist Watch. The Residential Edge Homes and small farms.
Name Description The Millstone Inn The only true inn in town. Clean and functional. The Waypost Tavern A rougher tavern for supply crews and garrison liaisons.

Azriel Population ~85,000 Type Capital city Region North-central, on Crown Lake Governance The Crown; five-seat council; the Crown Mage Garrison Royal Guard, ~8,000 Notable sites The Royal Palace, the Crown Mage's Tower, the Hall of Records, the Royal Academy Azriel is the capital of the Kingdom of Zeref and the seat of its crown, council, and highest military and magical authority. It stands on the northwest shore of Crown Lake, where the King's River begins. Maren I laid the city out as five concentric rings around the royal citadel, with wealth and rank thinning at every ring outward from the center. Magic is a common sight in Azriel to a degree found nowhere else in the kingdom. Lamplighters, bakers, and merchants all work minor magic as a matter of routine, and Arcanum Row in the Merchant Ring is the only street in the kingdom where arcane goods are sold openly and in volume.

Entertainment and cheap lodging.

Arcanum Row Four arcane establishments on one street in the Merchant Ring. The Entertainment Quarter Theatres, fighting pits, and gambling dens in the Outer City. See The People of Lorandal for the royal court and the council.

Coppergate Population ~7,000 Type Mining supply town Region World Spine foothills, Spineback River Governance Administrator Edran Voss Notable sites Gearwright's Workshop, the Humming Tunnel Coppergate is a mining town in the foothills of the World Spine, on the Spineback River, built to supply the deep operations that work the shafts and galleries the dwarves first cut thousands of years ago. It takes its name from the copper that built it. The gnome engineers of the Engineers' Quarter are the town's technical authority, and everything else in Coppergate exists to support the mines. The town is loud, practical, and permanently dusty.

Miners who have worked Coppergate's deepest galleries tell of a worked-out tunnel, far down in the old dwarven works, that the crews give a wide berth. There is a dark stone at the end of it, and the deepest miners say the rock down there is never quite silent. No survey has ever explained the sound, and the oldest maps mark the spot with only a question.

District Description The Upper Town Homes, the general market, and the main inn. The Engineers' Quarter The gnome engineering workshops. The Mine Approach The road to the mine entrance, equipment staging, and the healer's clinic.

Name District Description The Copper Tap Upper Town The main inn. Loud at shift change, quiet at dawn. The Deep Shift Mine Approach The working tavern nearest the mine entrance. The Engineers' Hall Engineers' Quarter A common house for the engineering staff.

Establishment Trade The Saltwright Apothecary, specializing in mining injuries Coppergate Steel Smith; tools and reinforced picks Gearwright's Workshop Engineering; keeps the mines running Mine Healer's Clinic Treats the injuries of a working mine town

Crestfall Population ~3,800 Type Administrative crossroads Region North of Azriel Known for Constant royal messenger traffic Crestfall stands at the crossing of the Northern Road and the Mist Road, north of Azriel, and royal messengers pass through it without pause. As a result its ordinary townsfolk are among the best-informed common people in the Kingdom about what the crown is doing, often hearing of a decree before it reaches the city it was addressed to. The Northern Road runs on from here to Stormhaven; the Mist Road, to the border garrisons.

Crossfen Population ~9,000 Type River confluence town Region The southern rivers Known for A halfling river-trade network Crossfen sits where the King's River meets the Marketh, a natural trade junction that by rights should be a larger city than it is. Much of its commerce moves through a halfling river network, and it is the usual point where Southern Reach goods coming up from Tidefall enter the river corridor. Upriver lies Redcross; downriver, the coast and Saltmere.

East Gate Population ~6,500 Type Frontier garrison and trade checkpoint Region The World Spine frontier Known for The overland Ketharan trade East Gate is a frontier town on the World Spine, half garrison and half trade checkpoint. Ketharan goods brought overland enter the Kingdom here, passing under the eye of a garrison that keeps a wary watch on the mountain trails, where raids by mountain goblins are a regular fact of the posting. It is the easternmost of the frontier towns, out beyond the mines worked from Coppergate.

Harrow Population ~3,200 Type Farming village Region The eastern plains Known for A hardy winter wheat Harrow is an almost entirely agricultural village on the open plains south of Mirror Lake, halfling-majority and known for a hardy winter wheat no other part of the Kingdom can grow. Nothing much happens in Harrow, which is exactly how Harrow likes it. It sits south of Sunfall and Mirror Lake, in the Kingdom's eastern farmland.

Ironhold Population ~22,000 Type Dwarven mining city Region Royal Hills, Goldrun River Governance Governor Dura Stonekeep Notable sites The Temple of Moradin Ironhold is the only city in the Kingdom of Zeref where dwarves outnumber everyone else, and it has built its whole identity on a single fact: when the greater part of the dwarves left for the east in the Kingdom's earliest years, the dwarves of Ironhold stayed. It is a mining city on the Goldrun River, and it has never let anyone forget the choice its founders made. The city is built for permanence: low ceilings, massive walls, and stonework meant to outlast its makers. The Temple of Moradin, the most active in the kingdom, is its religious, cultural, and communal center. Non-dwarves are received with cool professional tolerance and mostly live in the Surface Town.

District Description The Deep Quarter The dwarven cultural heart, home to the Temple of Moradin. The Working District The city's mining and crafting economy. The Surface Town The mixed residential layer, where most non-dwarves live.

Name District Description The Stone & Ale Deep Quarter The best rooms in the city, and ale that draws dwarves from across the kingdom. The Surface Rest Surface Town Where non-dwarves feel relatively welcome. The Forge Tap Working District A craftsmen's tavern with no patience for outsiders who talk too much.
Location Description The Temple of Moradin The most active Moradin temple in the kingdom. Governor Stonekeep's Hall Maintains the fastest channel between Ironhold and the capital's archives.

Karth Population ~42,000 Type Coastal port city Region Western coast, Golden Harbor Governance Crown-appointed governor; merchant guilds Garrison 14 warships, ~5,600 naval personnel Notable sites The Golden Lighthouse, the Temple of Lyssa, the Festival Ground Karth is the busiest port in the Kingdom of Zeref, and for anyone arriving by sea it is usually the first stretch of the Kingdom they stand on. It sits on the northern shore of Golden Harbor; most of the continent's sea traffic crosses its docks, and the yearly elven trade ship from Arendale makes its landing here. A crown-appointed governor shares power, not always comfortably, with the merchant guilds who run the waterfront. The city has two faces. The Golden Harbor district is polished and wealthy, all whitewashed counting-houses, guild halls, and deep-keeled ships from every coast. Twenty minutes inland the streets narrow into something crowded and ordinary. So much of the city is from somewhere else, or trading with somewhere else, that a stranger draws no particular attention. Karth sits about ninety miles from the Iron Pass, the northern gateway into the Greylands, close enough that news from the pass garrisons reaches it within days.
Pell Ashwick, Crown Mage of Karth Sergeant Brennan Morse, of the watch at the north gate Sorath, a stranger who appeared at the north gate

District Description Golden Harbor District The wealthy waterfront. Counting-houses, guild halls, the customs wharf, the lighthouse, and the governor's hall. The Wharfside The working waterfront. Docks, warehouses, the fish market, and dockworker taverns. The Inland Town The residential heart of the city. Markets, homes, the watch barracks, and most of Karth's inns. The Outer City The poor inland edge. Cheap lodging and the entertainment quarter. The Drift A self-governing foreign pocket built up over centuries. Boarding houses and taverns serving food no other quarter in the west can offer. North Gate Approach The landward threshold facing the farmland of the Harbor Plains.

Name District Description The Salted Anchor Inland Town A halfling-kept inn run by Mira Clover. Good food, fair prices, open late. The Anchor & Crown Golden Harbor A high-end inn favored by merchant captains. The Crossing House Inland Town A travelers' inn near the south road. The Drowned Lantern Wharfside A dockworker tavern known for having the freshest harbor news. The Broken Net Wharfside The sailor dive nearest the water. The Hundred Flags The Drift A foreign-run boarding house for sailors of every race. The Far Table The Drift A tavern serving dishes from across the seas.

Establishment Trade Brennan's Steel Smith, Inland Town Coir & Keel Ship-fitter and chandler; the busiest shop on the waterfront The Lamp & Glass Arcane sundries, scrolls, and components The Saltwright Apothecary and healing potions Temple of Lyssa Infirmary Temple healing The Harbor Market Daily market, with the widest foreign selection in the west

Location Description The Golden Lighthouse Guards the harbor mouth. Tended by an old keeper said to notice what others miss. The Temple of Lyssa The city's grand temple of the goddess of luck, and the center of Karth's Blue Moon Festival. The Festival Ground A plaza built for the Blue Moon Festival. The Stone Circle A ring of standing stones on the Harbor Plains, older than Karth. Local farmers leave it alone. The Black Stone A weathered standing stone of black rock out on the Harbor Plains, beyond the north gate. It predates the city; the farmers plough around it and leave it at that. The Governor's Hall The seat of crown authority in Karth. The North Gate The landward gate facing the Harbor Plains.

Millhaven Population ~14,000 Type River confluence town Region King's River and Goldrun River confluence Governance Administrator Coll Branwick; the halfling merchant council Notable sites The Two Rivers Inn, Poppy Thistledown's Hall Millhaven has governed itself for most of the Kingdom's history. When the crown chose to pour its coin into Varenholm instead, centuries ago, the town's old halfling and merchant families simply took up every role the crown never staffed, and never let go of them. It sits at the meeting of the King's River and the Goldrun River. The town answers to Administrator Coll Branwick in name; the people who actually decide things are Poppy Thistledown and the halfling merchant council, and most residents would struggle to name the administrator at all. Millhaven has no Crown Mage and no meaningful garrison, and remains one of the most stable settlements in the kingdom regardless.

District Description The Confluence The commercial heart, where the rivers meet. The Halfling Quarter The residential and cultural core. The Thornwood Edge The town's border with the Grey Wood, and its timber yards.

Name District Description The Two Rivers Inn Confluence The main inn, with the best food in Millhaven. The Halfling Arms Halfling Quarter A community inn; outsiders welcome when vouched for. The Barge & Barrel Confluence A working riverside tavern.

Location Description Poppy Thistledown's Hall The seat of the halfling merchant council, and the town's real government. Willa Burrows' House Home of Millhaven's oldest elder, well over a century old.

Mist Watch Population ~2,800 Type Border garrison Region The Fey Wood border Known for Watching the Mist Gate No one asks to be posted to Mist Watch. It is a border garrison town facing the Mist Gate, the guarded threshold of the Fey Wood: mostly soldiers, with only a few hundred civilians, set down at the edge of a forest most of the Kingdom never sees. The Fey Wood stands close to the west, its treeline within sight of the town's own walls. It is supplied from Ashford, further south along the Mist Road.

Redcross Population ~5,500 Type Bridge and toll town Region The King's River Known for A bridge three thousand years old Redcross is a toll town built around one of the oldest bridges on the King's River, a span three thousand years old. It takes its living from the crossing toll and its pride from the river corridor it belongs to, and its bridge masters have kept a record of every repair the bridge has needed across its whole long history. It stands on the river between Varenholm and Crossfen. Some travelers claim that at midnight on the winter solstice, standing at the center of the bridge, you can hear faint voices carried on the wind, and then nothing. People have told the story for centuries; no one has ever explained it.

Saltmere Population ~24,000 Type Naval base city Region Southern coast, Saltmere Fen Governance Fleet Admiral Cort Dunwall; Governor Pavan Maren Garrison 28 warships, ~11,200 naval personnel Notable sites The Naval Academy, Fleet Admiral's HQ Saltmere is the home port of the Kingdom's fleet, set where the Southrun River spreads into the brackish Saltmere Fen that shelters its anchorage. The city is naval in culture as much as in numbers: twenty-eight warships and some eleven thousand personnel are based here, and Fleet Admiral Cort Dunwall outranks the civilian governor in every way that matters. The Naval Academy is the city's intellectual center, training the kingdom's battle-mages, navigation officers, and marine tacticians. Saltmere is also the seat of worship of Maritha, the Anchored Tide, the patron goddess of the coast's knightly houses; see The Pantheon of Lorandal.

District Description The Naval Quarter The warship berths, the Naval Academy, and fleet command. The Supply District The logistics backbone of the fleet. The Civilian Town The city's non-naval residents.

Name District Description The Admiral's Berth Naval Quarter The senior officers' inn; visiting commanders, few civilians. The Salt Dog Civilian Town Where the real fleet news travels. The Fen & Flag Civilian Town The main civilian inn.

Location Description The Naval Academy The training ground of the kingdom's naval officers and battle-mages. Fleet Admiral's HQ The command center of the southern fleet. The Naval Hospital The fleet's medical heart.

Stormhaven Population ~18,000 Type Northern port Region Northern coast, Storm Sea Governance Governor Edric Vane; Fleet Commander Mira Stormcall Garrison 12 warships, ~4,800 naval personnel Notable sites The Ketharan Trade Dock, the Preserved Goods Market Stormhaven is the Kingdom's only port on the Storm Sea, and it lives its year in two halves: a five-month summer of open trade, when Ketharan ships make the crossing and the harbor fills, and a six-month winter, when the Storm Sea closes and the city turns inward on its stores. Winter has shaped everything about Stormhaven. Its larders are stocked with herring smoked to last a year, its houses are built to hold heat rather than to impress, and a town that spends six months snowed in together keeps closer than most. Fleet Commander Mira Stormcall holds the real authority over the crossing; her office sets the single annual departure window for the summer voyage to Kethara.
District Description The Harbor The summer-active waterfront and Ketharan arrival point. The Town The residential and commercial core. The Winter Quarter The community warehouses and winter market.

Name District Description The Storm & Anchor Harbor The best inn in town; hosts the Ketharan traders each summer. The Long Winter Town A travelers' inn built for endurance. The Hearthside Town The town's common room through the winter months.

Location Description Mira Stormcall's Navigation Office Holds the Storm Sea charts and sets the annual crossing window. The Preserved Goods Market Smoked herring that keeps a year, salt-packed meats, and the rest of the kingdom's best preserved food. The Ketharan Trade Dock Active only during the summer window.

Sunfall Population ~11,000 Type Lakeside town Region Mirror Lake, eastern Kingdom Known for Fishing, farming, and the view at dawn Sunfall is a fishing and farming town on the western shore of Mirror Lake. The lake is genuinely mirror-still, and travelers will go out of their way to see the town at first light. Beyond the view, Sunfall is a mainstay of the Kingdom's eastern food supply. It lies near the farming village of Harrow and the mining town of Coppergate, in the Kingdom's eastern country.

Tidefall Population ~28,000 Type Southern trade port Region Southern coast, Southrun River mouth Governance Governor Lira Vane; cooperative guilds Notable sites The Dragon Sea Dock, the Southern Market, the Temple of the Deep Tidefall is the Kingdom's southern gateway, the port where the Southern Reach first meets Lorandal. It stands at the mouth of the Southrun River and is the most cosmopolitan city in the realm: its permanent Foreign Quarter houses Southern Reach traders and a long-established tortle community, and some ten thousand sailors and merchants pass through at any given time. Smaller than Karth but wealthier per head, it keeps its harbor noticeably cleaner. The city faces the Dragon Sea, and its sailors treat that water with respect. Voyages east are rare, and the names of those lost to the crossing are carved into a memorial wall near the dock. Tidefall also serves as the Kingdom's winter port for the Kethara trade, when the calmer Southern Reach route is preferred over the Storm Sea. The city is governed by Lira Vane, who has a reputation for seeing straight through people; petitioners quickly learn that complete honesty is the only approach that works with her.

District Description Harbor Front The commercial waterfront. The customs dock, the shipyard, and the sailors' memorial wall. Merchant Quarter The business and residential heart of the city. Foreign Quarter The permanent, prosperous home of the Southern Reach community. Temple and Civic District The city's finest public institutions. Outer Streets The rough edge of an otherwise gentle city.

Name District Description The Coral Court Foreign Quarter The most lavish lodging outside Azriel, Southern Reach in style. The Dragon's Wake Harbor Front A famous sailors' dive where Dragon Sea crews drink. The Tide's Rest Merchant Quarter A solid mid-tier inn. The Southern Star Foreign Quarter Southern Reach cuisine no other kitchen in the kingdom serves.

Establishment Trade Deepwater Yards Shipyard; builds and repairs Dragon Sea vessels The Iron Tide Outfitter Specialist voyage gear for the eastern crossing The Southern Market Spices, tropical materials, and southern goods Coin & Tide Money-changer

Location Description The Dragon Sea Dock The departure point for the rare voyage onto the Dragon Sea. The Sailors' Memorial Wall The names of every Dragon Sea sailor lost, carved in stone near the dock. The Foreign Quarter Plaza The elder Shell-of-Still-Waters holds court here most mornings. He is older than kingdom records. The Temple of the Deep The city's primary temple and a great house of Melora, goddess of the sea. Every Dragon Sea voyage begins with an offering here. The Governor's Hall The seat of Governor Lira Vane. The city's Crown Mage is Fenn Ashoral, and the harbor taverns are full of retired Dragon Sea sailors with stories to sell.

Varenholm Population ~38,000 Type River crossing city Region The King's River Governance Governor Brynn Coppervein; merchant guilds Notable sites The King's River Bridge, the Commodity Exchange, the grain warehouses Varenholm is the commercial heart of the Kingdom of Zeref, built where the King's River narrows to its most crossable point. The stone-arched King's River Bridge, three thousand years old and wide enough for two wagons abreast, is the reason the city exists, and its toll bells can be heard before the city comes into view. The city's Commodity Exchange sets the prices of grain, timber, metals, and textiles for the entire kingdom. Varenholm also holds twelve months of regional grain reserves in a heavily guarded warehouse row, making it the kingdom's second food pillar after the royal granaries of Azriel. Governor Brynn Coppervein, a dwarf, holds the bridge tolls; the merchant guilds hold the Exchange; and the two run the city between them. They cooperate because disagreement is bad for business.

District Description Bridge District The crossing and its commerce. The bridge, the toll gates, and the governor's hall. Merchant Quarter The Commodity Exchange, the grain market, and the guild seat. The Riverside The working waterfront. Docks, grain warehouses, and barge crews' taverns. Inland Town The residential quarter.

Name District Description The Crossed Keys Bridge District A grand merchants' inn; the address for serious traders. The River & Rye Riverside The gathering place for barge crews and river merchants. The Grain & Flagon Inland Town An honest inn run by and for working folk. The Wayfarers' Rest Inland Town A road-house for travelers passing through.

Location Description The King's River Bridge The kingdom's oldest working crossing, toll-gated at both ends. The Bridge-Keeper's Lodge The toll and record office, with crossing records going back centuries. The Commodity Exchange The commercial engine of the kingdom. The Grain Warehouses Twelve months of regional reserves under permanent guard. The Temple of the Exchange The commerce god's temple, where merchants pray before major deals.

Background on the world of Lorandal: its lands and history, the gods its peoples keep, the powers that divide the continent, and the great festival on the horizon. Page About The World The three continents, the Elder Tree, and the shape of the world. History of the Kingdom The founding, the royal line, and the long story of the Kingdom of Zeref. The Blue Moon Festival The once-in-500-years festival, and the five that came before. Factions of Lorandal The Kingdom, the elves of the Fey Wood, and the Greylands. The Greylands The clans behind the Iron Wall, Grimhold, and the two passes. The Pantheon of Lorandal The gods of the founding races and the faiths kept today. The Peoples of Lorandal The races of the Kingdom, and the eastern realm of Kethara.

Lorandal is the main continent of the known world, about 700 miles east to west and 500 miles north to south. The Kingdom of Zeref controls almost all of it. Two other continents are known: Kethara across the eastern sea, and an unnamed western landmass that no expedition has ever successfully explored.

Continent Name Status Notes Main Lorandal Controlled almost entirely by the Kingdom of Zeref The Fey Wood, in the northwest, is the exception. Eastern Kethara A meritocratic senate of six races Reachable by ship from Tidefall or Stormhaven. Western Unnamed Barren and unmapped Explorers rarely return. Those who do refuse to describe what they found.

Deep inside the Fey Wood stands the Elder Tree, held by the elves as the most sacred site in the world. Almost nothing is known about it in the Kingdom. Its age, its nature, and the reason for its sanctity are all questions without answers; whatever was once known has been lost, and the elves do not discuss the Tree with outsiders. Its location has never been charted, and the forest itself is commonly said to hide it. No outsider has ever claimed to have stood before it and been believed.
Each of the founding races honors its own patron god, and the faiths remain part of daily life across the Kingdom. See The Pantheon of Lorandal.

Three powers divide the continent of Lorandal: the Kingdom of Zeref, which holds nearly all of it; the elves of the Fey Wood in the northwest; and the clans of the Greylands, sealed behind the Iron Wall in the southwest.

Founded Crown Year 0, by King Zeref Territory All of Lorandal except the Fey Wood Population ~5.2 million Government Hereditary monarchy with crown-appointed governors Military ~52,000 standing The Kingdom of Zeref has been ruled by a single hereditary human bloodline for three thousand years. There is no hereditary nobility below the crown; every city and town answers to a crown-appointed governor. The King's court is organized around five council seats, one for each of the founding races except the elves, with a single Crown Mage above them all who answers only to the monarch. See King Aldric Zeref and The Council of Azriel. Magic is unregulated throughout the Kingdom and treated as a skilled trade. Roughly one person in five can manage simple cantrip-level effects. The cities along the King's River, from Azriel south through Varenholm, Millhaven, Redcross, Tidefall, and Saltmere, generate most of the Kingdom's commercial revenue and are known for saying so.

The elves have lived apart in the Fey Wood since the Kingdom's earliest years. The law separating the two peoples is three thousand years old, and the reason it was made has been lost on both sides of the border; the elves are said to remember an ancient betrayal, but few alive could say what it truly was. Almost nothing about elven society is known in the Kingdom with certainty. Settlement What is known Moonveil The elven capital. Known by name only; no outsider has seen it. Gold Leaf The seat of the elven Council of Elders. Known mainly through the river that carries its name out of the forest. Arendale A coastal trade town, and the only elven settlement whose existence the Kingdom has confirmed. The Fey Wood resists mapping, and the elven coast along The Veil is permanently wrapped in mist. How many elves live beyond the treeline is unknown. Once a year, one elven ship sails from Arendale to Karth and one Kingdom ship sails the reverse route, on a date set jointly by the Crown and the Council of Elders. If either ship fails to return, the agreement is permanently broken. See Arendale.
documents.s: The elves of the Fey Wood

documents.t: Territory The southwest peninsula, behind the Iron Wall Peoples Hobgoblins, bugbears, gnolls, lizardfolk Government A council of clan leaders at Grimhold The peoples of the Greylands were pushed behind the Iron Wall when the Kingdom's borders were drawn, and the land they hold has grown poorer every generation since. Raids across the two mountain passes, Iron Pass in the north and Stone Pass in the south, are a fact of life on the frontier; the pass garrisons have held against them for three thousand years. Reports from the garrisons describe four clans, governed by a council whose members seldom pull the same way. See The Greylands for the region, its stronghold at Grimhold, and the passes. Clan People Reputation at the passes Iron Clan Hobgoblins Disciplined and military-minded Raid Clan Bugbears Opportunistic raiders Stone Clan Gnolls Zealous and unpredictable Old Clan Lizardfolk Rarely seen at the passes at all

The Greylands Territory The southwestern peninsula, behind the Iron Wall Peoples Hobgoblins, bugbears, gnolls, lizardfolk Population ~60,000 to 80,000 Stronghold Grimhold The Greylands are the blighted southwestern peninsula, sealed off from the rest of Lorandal by the Iron Wall. The land is poor and grows poorer with every generation, and the peoples who hold it live largely by raiding across the mountain passes into the Kingdom, because their own soil no longer feeds them. Somewhere between sixty and eighty thousand live here, of whom perhaps eight to ten thousand are fighters, governed, loosely, by a council of four clan leaders that rarely agrees on anything. See also Factions of Lorandal.

The Iron Wall is not a built wall but a mountain range, running coast to coast across the neck of the peninsula and anchored to the sea at both ends. There is no way around it. Two passes cut through it, Iron Pass in the north and Stone Pass in the south, and the Kingdom's garrisons have held both against Greylands raids for three thousand years.

Grimhold is the central stronghold of the Greylands, seated on the Blood River, and the meeting place of the clan council. What the Kingdom knows of it comes secondhand, through the pass garrisons: no kingdom force has ever marched on it, and few outsiders have ever seen it and come back to describe it.

The northern of the two passes through the Iron Wall, held by a Kingdom garrison tower of some six hundred soldiers. Being the further of the two from Grimhold, it sees the lighter share of the raiding.

The southern pass, and the harder posting. Its garrison of roughly a thousand takes the brunt of Greylands raiding, being the nearer to Grimhold, and the gatehouse wall carries a tally of every successful defense, thousands of marks deep. A soldier's first repelled raid there is a rite of passage.

The Kingdom of Zeref was founded three thousand years ago and has been ruled by a single unbroken royal line ever since. Most of what happened before and during the founding era has been lost; the record below is what the Kingdom itself teaches and keeps.

According to the Kingdom's histories, a darkness rose in the age before the founding and nearly consumed the world. King Zeref led the peoples of Lorandal against it and broke it, and founded the Kingdom on the strength of that victory. He named it after himself while still alive, and is remembered as its founding hero. Founding Day, held each spring, still honors him. What the darkness actually was, no surviving record says. The oldest accounts are fragmentary or contradictory, and three thousand years of retelling have worn the story into legend. The blighted expanse of the Ash Fields is popularly believed to date from that era, though no one can say for certain what happened there. The Kingdom's first years also saw two departures whose reasons are equally lost. The elves withdrew, or were driven, into the Fey Wood, and the law separating them from the Kingdom dates from that time and has never been repealed. The greater part of the dwarves left Lorandal entirely, crossing the eastern sea to found what became Kethara. The elves are said to remember an ancient betrayal from this period, but few alive, on either side of the border, could say what it truly was.

Monarch Crown Years Notes Zeref I, the Founder 0 to ~35 Broke the darkness, founded the Kingdom, and named it after himself. Aldran I, the Inheritor ~35 to 68 The first king born after the founding. Made the banishment of the elves into settled law. Maren I, the Builder ~68 to 95 Built Azriel's concentric rings and the King's Road. Aldran II ~370 to 408 Reigned during the first Blue Moon Festival. Voran II, the Pious ~408 to 441 Declared the blue moon a blessing of Lyssa by royal decree. Edran III, the Patron ~890 to 924 Founded the Royal Academy. Reigned during the second Blue Moon Festival. Aldran III, the Grand ~1370 to 1408 Reigned during the third Blue Moon Festival. Standardized the festival's blue lanterns and banners. Voran III, the Stable ~1480 to 1515 The most peaceful reign on record. Maren II, the Merchant ~1870 to 1905 Reigned during the fourth Blue Moon Festival, at the height of the Kingdom's recorded wealth. Eryndas I, the Scholar ~2240 to 2275 Commissioned a great audit of the Kingdom's historical records. Aldran IV, the Long ~2332 to 2401 The longest reign in Kingdom history, at 69 years. Reigned during the fifth Blue Moon Festival. Voran IV, the Cautious ~2620 to 2651 Built the pass fortifications facing the Greylands that the army still relies on. Edran IV, the Beloved ~2800 to 2835 Grandfather of the current king. Known for walking Azriel's outer rings without a guard. Davan Zeref, the Stable ~2860 to 2890 Father of the current king. Thirty years of steady rule. Aldric Zeref ~2890 to present The reigning king. See King Aldric Zeref.

For most of the Kingdom's history there was no contact with the Fey Wood at all. The old hostility has thawed only in recent centuries: rare elves are now permitted among men, and the annual trade between Karth and Arendale is the one formal link between the two peoples. See Factions of Lorandal.

The peoples of Lorandal keep a broad and living faith. Each of the founding races honors its own creator god, and above and alongside them stands a wider pantheon worshipped across the whole Kingdom of Zeref.

Each founding race was made, by its own tradition, in the image of its god, and those gods are still honored today. Race God Domain Worship today Elves Corellon Larethian Arcana, beauty, magic Still honored in kingdom temples, though the link to the banished elves goes largely unremarked Dwarves Moradin The forge, creation, family Strongest at Ironhold; the most active shrines of all are cut into the World Spine mines Halflings Yondalla Life, hearth, community Woven deep into daily life; many halfling homes keep a small Yondalla shelf by the door Orcs Gruumsh Strength, endurance The Elder Tree orcs reformed his worship, honoring his strength without his rage Gnomes Garl Glittergold Trickery, gems, protection Active in gnome communities; the gnomes of Coppergate pray to him before opening any new shaft Humans The wider pantheon All of the below Humans claim no single creator and worship freely across the gods below

These gods are honored across the Kingdom, by every race. God Domain Symbol Worship in Lorandal Lyssa Luck, change, travel Three coins on a cord Goddess of travelers, merchants, and the unlucky. Kingdom folk credit her with the blue moon. "Lyssa" is the common folk name; older temple texts call her Avandra. Pelor Sun, life, healing A radiant sun disk The Kingdom's dominant healing god. Most temples are Pelor-primary, and his clerics are the most common divine callers in the realm. Ioun Knowledge, prophecy, skill A crook-headed staff Patron of Crown Mages, scholars, and scribes. Melora Nature, sea, wilderness A cresting wave Goddess of the fisher-towns and farming villages. Her great temples stand at Tidefall and Arendale. The Raven Queen Death, fate, memory A raven over a mask The just and neutral goddess of death. Death rites across every race invoke her, though she keeps no formal church. Bahamut Justice, protection, honor A dragon in profile The lawful god of paladins and city guards. Maritha, the Anchored Tide Law, protection, the sea An anchor embraced by a cresting wave A regional goddess of the southern coast, worshipped by the Tritons of Saltmere, the coastal noble houses, and naval knights. Sehanine Moonbow The moon, illusion, secrets A crescent moon The elven moon goddess, also honored in halfling communities.

The great Blue Moon Festival is bound up with faith. Kingdom folk have credited Lyssa with the omen since a royal decree made it official centuries ago. The elves credit their own moon goddess, Sehanine Moonbow, instead. Both beliefs are old and sincerely held. See The Blue Moon Festival.

Holiday Faith Season Observed The Blue Moon Festival Lyssa Every 500 years Worldwide The Harvest Feast Yondalla Late autumn Kingdom-wide; the most observed holiday after the Blue Moon Founding Day Secular Early spring Kingdom-wide, honoring King Zeref The Long Night Mixed Winter solstice Kingdom-wide; candles burned for the dead The Soldier's Rest Secular Midsummer Military cities The River Run Secular Late summer The King's River corridor Forgeday Moradin Midwinter Primarily Ironhold The Inventor's Fair Garl Glittergold Spring Gnome communities

The Kingdom of Zeref has been race-blind in law for three thousand years. In practice, its population reflects its history: humans form the majority everywhere, elves are vanishingly rare, and Ironhold is the one city where dwarves outnumber everyone else. People Share of the Kingdom Notes Humans 54% The majority in every region. Dwarves 16% Concentrated in Ironhold; descended from those who stayed when the rest departed east. Halflings 11% Common in the river towns and farming country. Gnomes 8% Took over the dwarves' abandoned mines and became the kingdom's underground engineers. Half-orcs 6% Common in military towns and garrisons. Orcs ~4% Settled throughout the kingdom. Tieflings 2% Face a quiet social wariness that nobody has ever adequately explained. Dragonborn 1.5% Descended from arrivals from Kethara. Elves 0.6% Extremely rare; concentrated near Arendale. Half-elves 0.3% Rarer still, and belonging fully to neither society. Tritons Under 0.1% Sea-folk of the far southern waters, settled almost entirely around Saltmere, where a few families have risen into the naval nobility.

People Custom Humans Last rites led by clerics of the Raven Queen, consecrated burial, and seven days of mourning. Dwarves Burial within the mountain. A dwarf buried in open ground is considered lost. Halflings Three days of stories held as a community event. An empty place is kept at the table on anniversaries. Orcs and half-orcs Warriors are buried with their weapons. The name is spoken aloud on each anniversary. Gnomes Cremation. The ashes feed a tree planted in the deceased's name. Elves Return to the Fey Wood for burial in consecrated forest ground. An elf who cannot be returned is considered lost. Tieflings No unified tradition; local custom is generally adopted. Dragonborn Formal recitation of the deceased's achievements, then cremation. Scales are preserved and passed down.

The greater part of the dwarves left Lorandal in the Kingdom's earliest years, for reasons long lost, and together with the peoples already living across the eastern sea built Kethara: a unified state governed by a meritocratic senate of six races (dwarves, aarakocra, loxodon, genasi, tortle, and yuan-ti). Its relationship with the Kingdom of Zeref is commercial and correct, but has never been warm. Trade runs through Stormhaven in summer and Tidefall in winter.

Once every 500 years the moon rises blue for a single night, and the world stops to celebrate it. The priesthood of Lyssa, goddess of luck, has claimed the omen as hers for as long as records go back, and the festival held under the blue light has grown into the largest celebration anyone knows: lanterns in every window, banners down every street, and a wish made, by tradition, by the whole world at once. Five blue moons have risen since the Kingdom was founded. Festival Crown Year Notes 1st ~400 The first blue moon of the Kingdom's era. 2nd ~900 Lyssa's priests claimed the omen as hers; the festival tradition dates from this night. 3rd ~1,400 The blue lanterns and banners still used today were introduced under Aldran III. 4th ~1,900 The grandest festival then on record. The Crown made it an official holiday. 5th ~2,400 The most recent. Nobody alive remembers it firsthand. Every almanac in the Kingdom puts the next blue moon within the current generation, and preparations for the greatest festival in its history have been underway for years.
